AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #16 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which is a benefit of compost to sandy soil? (1 mark)
   A. It makes the soil disappear
   B. It removes all nutrients
   C. It helps the soil to hold water
   D. It makes the soil more sandy

2. About how long does compost usually take to be ready? (1 mark)
   A. Two years
   B. Ten minutes
   C. Two to three months
   D. One day

3. Why do we sprinkle soil or old compost between layers? (1 mark)
   A. It adds plastic
   B. It keeps birds away
   C. It adds tiny living things that help wastes to rot
   D. It makes the heap sweeter

4. What is the purpose of sticks at the bottom of the compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. They make it look neat
   B. They keep the heap dry forever
   C. They let air move through the heap
   D. They add plant food

5. Why is a cloth placed over the opening of the water container? (1 mark)
   A. To keep dirt from blocking the small holes
   B. To make the water hot
   C. To colour the water
   D. To make the container heavier

6. What is the meaning of conserving water? (1 mark)
   A. Storing dirty water
   B. Selling water
   C. Using as much as possible
   D. Using it carefully so none is wasted

7. Why should the end of the drip pipe be closed? (1 mark)
   A. So rainwater cannot enter
   B. So water does not run out of the end
   C. So the pipe looks nice
   D. So the plants do not drink

8. How far from the plant should the bottle drip be placed? (1 mark)
   A. About 10 to 15 cm
   B. In the next field
   C. Two metres
   D. Exactly on top of the stem

9. What does it mean to conserve fuel? (1 mark)
   A. To hide it
   B. To waste it
   C. To use only what is needed and make it last
   D. To burn as much as possible

10. Which action wastes fuel? (1 mark)
   A. Turning the flame down after boiling starts
   B. Using a lid
   C. Using dry wood
   D. Boiling water with no lid and a big flame

11. Why should you prepare all the food before lighting the fire? (1 mark)
   A. So the fire does not burn while you are still preparing
   B. To make the food colder
   C. To use more wood
   D. To cook faster than a cooker

12. Which of these is a fuel used at home for cooking? (1 mark)
   A. Charcoal
   B. Sand
   C. Glass
   D. Cloth

13. What is used to make the arms of a scarecrow? (1 mark)
   A. A bucket of water
   B. A bottle
   C. Sand
   D. A shorter stick tied across the pole

14. Which is a way of conserving wild animals? (1 mark)
   A. Setting fires in the bush
   B. Selling them
   C. Protecting their homes such as forests
   D. Cutting down all trees

15. Where is a scarecrow best placed? (1 mark)
   A. At the river
   B. Inside the house
   C. Far from the crop
   D. In the middle or at the side of the crop where animals come from

16. Which is the best material for stuffing a scarecrow? (1 mark)
   A. Glass
   B. Stones
   C. Dry grass
   D. Wet mud

17. What should be done first before pulling out seedlings when thinning? (1 mark)
   A. Cut the tops off
   B. Dry the bed
   C. Water the bed so the soil is soft
   D. Cover it with plastic

18. Why do we label the seedbed rows? (1 mark)
   A. To scare birds
   B. To remember the crop and the date sown
   C. To give plants names
   D. To decorate

19. Why do crowded seedlings grow badly? (1 mark)
   A. They get too much space
   B. They like company
   C. They have no roots
   D. They compete for water, light and food

20. About how far apart may rows of tiny seeds be? (1 mark)
   A. 10 metres
   B. 1 mm
   C. 5 metres
   D. 15 to 20 cm

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain what thinning is and why it is done. (3 marks)

22. Name two other ways of saving water in the garden. (2 marks)

23. Describe how a family can plant trees to help conserve fuel. (4 marks)

24. Give three ways of caring for a drip irrigation system. (3 marks)

25. Name four fuels used for cooking in homes. (2 marks)

26. How can a school without land grow radish or amaranth? (3 marks)

27. List three materials that can be used to make a scarecrow. (3 marks)

28. Why should kerosene never be poured onto a fire? (2 marks)

29. List three things needed to make a bucket drip system. (3 marks)

30. Explain why drip irrigation is useful in a dry area and describe how a school could set up a system for a row of kale. (5 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #16 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — It helps the soil to hold water
   Compost holds water like a sponge.

2. C — Two to three months
   It depends on weather and materials but is usually two to three months.

3. C — It adds tiny living things that help wastes to rot
   Soil and old compost carry bacteria and fungi that break down wastes.

4. C — They let air move through the heap
   Air helps the tiny living things rot the wastes.

5. A — To keep dirt from blocking the small holes
   Dirt would clog the tiny holes.

6. D — Using it carefully so none is wasted
   Conserving means saving and protecting.

7. B — So water does not run out of the end
   An open end would waste water.

8. A — About 10 to 15 cm
   Close enough for the roots to reach the water.

9. C — To use only what is needed and make it last
   Conserving fuel means saving it.

10. D — Boiling water with no lid and a big flame
   Heat escapes without a lid and a big flame.

11. A — So the fire does not burn while you are still preparing
   Fuel is not wasted waiting.

12. A — Charcoal
   Charcoal is burnt to give heat.

13. D — A shorter stick tied across the pole
   The cross stick forms shoulders and arms.

14. C — Protecting their homes such as forests
   Protecting habitats lets animals live.

15. D — In the middle or at the side of the crop where animals come from
   It must be seen by the animals that come to the crop.

16. C — Dry grass
   Dry grass is light and easy to use.

17. C — Water the bed so the soil is soft
   Wet soil lets you pull gently without harming others.

18. B — To remember the crop and the date sown
   Labels prevent confusion.

19. D — They compete for water, light and food
   Too many plants in a small space fight for resources.

20. D — 15 to 20 cm
   Rows are close but leave space for weeding.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is removing extra seedlings. It gives the remaining plants space and reduces competition for water, light and food.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 2 marks for reasons.

22. (2 marks)
   Answer: Mulching, collecting rainwater, watering in the morning or evening, reusing wash water (any two).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: Plant fast growing trees on their land for firewood, care for them and replace any tree cut with more new trees, so wood is always available and forests are not cut.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for planting, caring, replacing and result.

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fill the container daily, check for leaks and blocked holes, keep the water covered and clean.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

25. (2 marks)
   Answer: Firewood, charcoal, gas and kerosene.
   Working / marking points: Half a mark for each fuel, total 2.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Use a box or tin with drainage holes filled with fine soil and compost; sow the seeds thinly; water gently and place in sunlight.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for container, sowing, care.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sticks or poles, old clothes, a sack, dry grass, string, tins, old CDs (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct material.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: It catches fire quickly and can burst into flames and burn people.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for catching fire, 1 mark for danger.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: A bucket or container, a hose or pipe, and small holes or drippers for water to come out. A stand may also be used.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each item.

30. (5 marks)
   Answer: It saves scarce water because water reaches roots directly and little is lost. For kale: raise a bucket on a stand, attach a hose along the row, close the end, ask an adult to make small holes beside each plant, fill with clean water and check that drips are slow.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for reasons, 3 marks for set-up steps.
